AI & automation

Schneider connects software-defined automation with AWS while retaining local control

EcoStruxure Automation Expert connects AI and edge services to support reusable applications across machines and sites.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗25 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

An SPS announcement

Schneider Electric announced Open Software-Defined Automation on AWS on November 25. EcoStruxure Automation Expert connects operational data with cloud, edge, AI and security services. The stated goal is to extend analytics and AI beyond isolated pilots to multiple machines and plants.

Separating software from hardware

Control applications are designed for reuse across compatible computing environments. Local function blocks connect capabilities built with Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker, while AWS IoT Greengrass supports software deployment across sites. The companies aim to reduce gateways, protocol converters and bespoke interfaces.

Time-critical work stays local

The architecture retains deterministic, time-critical control on the factory floor while cloud services support broader analytics and learning. Deployment still requires compatible environments and a clear division of responsibilities. The announcement does not provide quantified customer returns or performance benchmarks for this new solution.
